messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected on /v1/stream (region: us-west-2). SLO breach flagged (p99 > 1200ms). Auto-signal: streaming-stall. Rolling 5min window shows 4.8x baseline. Incident ID: INC-2026-3487 :rotating_light:

Alice M.: saw the alert coming in, looks correlated with a recent prefix-hash rollout at 02:10 UTC. Traces show cache-hit drop from ~88% -> 12% on paging layer.

Carla (on-call): on it. pinging infra team. Is there a quick rollback for the prefix-hash config?

Ben S.: I have the rollout PR number: deploy/rl-prefixhash-v3. Deployed automatically 02:08 by Deploy-Bot. Rolling back to v2 is possible but will require a config flip + minor restart on shard-proxy.

Deploy-Bot: Rollout deploy/rl-prefixhash-v3 completed at 02:08:32 by ci/cd. Canary passed health checks (3/3).

Carla (on-call): prioritizing customer impact. CS: any reported user errors?

Customer Success: 3 customers reported degraded streaming (partial frames, stalls). One enterprise tenant (acme-inc) reported timeouts in production, opened support ticket #6782. They are in us-west-2.

Evan R.: metrics dump from edge-proxy (snippet):
```
edge_proxy_stream_p95_us_west_2: 420ms -> 2100ms
edge_proxy_stream_p99_us_west_2: 850ms -> 4200ms
cache_prefetch_hit_rate_prefix_v3: 0.12
cache_prefetch_hit_rate_prefix_v2: 0.87
paging_eviction_rate: +3.1x
```

Alice M.: logs from prefix service show increased namespace churn after new hash mapping: many keys remapped to different buckets, causing cold reads and synchronous prefetch storms. Likely a Zipf/hotkey redistribution problem.

Carla (on-call): mitigation options: 1) rollback prefix-hash to v2 (fast, requires short proxy restart), 2) enable emergency cache-warming using previous namespace mapping (best-effort), 3) apply rate limit to streaming clients to reduce tail. I recommend rollback + cache-warm. Thoughts?

Ben S.: rollback plan: flip config flag in k8s configmap `prefix-hash-version: v2` in staging then prod. Requires shard-proxy restart with 30s rolling bounce. I can script the rollback: `kubectl patch cm prefix-config -n infra -p '{"data":{"prefix-hash-version":"v2"}}'` then `kubectl rollout restart deploy/shard-proxy -n infra`. Estimated 3-5 minutes to ramp to healthy.

SRE-Mgr: approve rollback. Execute and monitor p99. If rollback fails, fallback to prefetch buffer throttle.

Carla (on-call): executing rollback now. Ben, send the patch. Evan, stand by to watch p99/p95 and KV cache hit rate.

Ben S.: applying patch now. running:
```
# apply config
kubectl patch cm prefix-config -n infra -p '{"data":{"prefix-hash-version":"v2"}}'
# restart proxies
kubectl rollout restart deploy/shard-proxy -n infra
```

Deploy-Bot: Started rollout restart for deploy/shard-proxy at 02:20:12 UTC. 1/12 pods restarted. Health checks ongoing.

Evan R.: early signal: p99 dropping from 4200ms -> 1600ms on first pods. Hit rate rising on restarted pods: 0.36 -> 0.62.

Carla (on-call): good. continue. posting status to customers. @Customer Success prepare a note: we're mitigating and have initiated rollback, ETA 5-10m for full recovery.

Customer Success: crafting message. will include temporary increased latency and that a rollback is in progress. tagging acme-inc support.

Alice M.: added a temporary guard to prevent synchronous prefetch storms: limit `prefetch_concurrency` to 8 per shard via runtime flag. Applied to edge-proxy as a runtime override (no restart). Should reduce tail while full rollback completes.

Evan R.: by 02:26UTC global p99 stable at ~380ms, us-west-2 p99 at ~520ms. Cache hit rate trending to 0.71. No additional customer error reports in last 10m.

Carla (on-call): marking live-mitigation in place. assigning followup tasks: 1) Postmortem owner, 2) Investigate why canary allowed v3 to push (hash distribution test gap), 3) Improve pre-deploy simulation for hotkey skew.

SRE-Mgr: Postmortem owner assigned to Alice M. Please include timeline, customer impact (list of tenants), root cause (prefix-hash remapping + hotkey concentration), and corrective actions (rollback gating, canary load profiles).

Ben S.: leaving handoff notes for next shift: rollback performed at 02:20 UTC, proxies restarted, temporary prefetch throttle applied. Watch for re-introducing v3 — do not redeploy until followup done.

Carla (on-call): handing off to night on-call @Evan R. for monitoring. Evan, check p95/p99, prefetch hit rate, and support tickets for 12h. if p99 > 800ms for >5m escalate.

Evan R.: ack. I will monitor dashboards and run a gradual re-warm job overnight to repopulate caches from historical prefixes (low-rate background jobs to avoid spikes).

Customer Success: notified affected customers at 02:28 UTC. acme-inc acknowledged and is monitoring. They requested ETA for full recovery — we told them 30m for finish warm.

Alice M.: initial RCA items: missing synthetic traffic profile during canary allowed v3 to pass; hash function stats not surfaced in CI; no automatic rollback trigger on hit-rate drop. Adding these to action list.

Carla (on-call): closing incident channel for live actions. Moving to incident followup doc INC-2026-3487 in confluence. If any regression or new spike, re-open thread. :white_check_mark:
